chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Marriage is not permissible today in Islam through wage (ijarah); if he says, 'I will work for you for such and such years on the condition that you marry me your daughter or your sister,' it is prohibited because it is the price of her neck, and she is more rightful to her dower.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage through wage or service (Ijarah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the prohibition of 'nikah al-ijarah' (marriage for wages), where a man works for a set period in exchange for marrying a woman, by ruling it haram because the woman is treated as a commodity with a fixed price rather than receiving her independent dower (mahr). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the woman herself is the rightful owner of her mahr, distinguishing this practice from standard marriage contracts where mahr is a gift or right rather than a direct wage for service. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that marriage must be a contract of consent and right, not a transactional exchange of labor for a person.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The marriage is not Permissible today in Al-Islam with wages, if he is saying, ‘I will work with you for such and such years upon a stipulation that you would marry your daughter, or your sister to me’. It is Prohibited because it would be a price for her neck, and she is more rightful with her dower’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Marriage is not lawful in Islam for hiring and saying, ‘I will work for you up to so and so many years and you give to me in marriage your daughter or sister.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is unlawful because it is the price of her neck and in fact she is the rightful person for her mahr (dower).”’
